task.description: HARD GATE. Independently validate lib/letflow/design/req023-event-store-schema.md (commit 2f7a8b8, 1184 lines) on branch feature/WF02-REQ023-20260816 against REQ-023's 5 acceptance criteria and WF-02 Step 1b's checklist (a-e). Read the design artefact directly and re-derive every verdict from primary sources -- do NOT read CODE-DESIGNER's handoff result.summary as a substitute for reading the artefact and the sources it cites. Pay particular attention to three things ORCH has already independently confirmed and which you must re-derive rather than take on trust: (1) the design claims REQ-022's shipped tenant_scoped_migrations/0 is defective and proposes fixing it inside this run -- verify that claim against deps/ecto_sql's actual Ecto.Migrator source and mix.exs, and judge whether the proposed fix is in scope (Unblock-Everything) or scope creep; (2) the design must specify the prefix() guard pattern REQ-022's design doc section 4 declares mandatory for every tenant-scoped migration, AND registration in tenant_scoped_migrations/0 -- REQ-022's design says both halves are mandatory and either alone is a defect; (3) the design deliberately omits a unique index on events.idempotency_key, which contradicts R-Co's own 001_event_store.sql and event_store.md invariant 4 -- verify this is genuinely required by 0003 Decision C point 2(b) and R-Co's 1147 migration rather than an unjustified divergence.
acceptance_criteria: priv/repo/migrations gains migrations for events, instance_sequence, event_payload_store, events_archive, the idempotency sidecar table, and instance_projections, all using Ecto's :prefix option and applying cleanly against at least one provisioned tenant schema via REQ-022's migration-replay mechanism
events' migration defines the primary key as (event_id, created_at), not a bare event_id, per 0003 Decision C point 2(a)

the events Ecto.Schema module has no update_changeset/2 or any function that issues an UPDATE against a committed row; the moduledoc states this is a deliberate immutability invariant per 0003 Decision C point 1
the idempotency sidecar table has a unique index on idempotency_key and its own moduledoc states it supersedes event_store.md's Open Question #1 two-phase-check recommendation per 0003's resolution
instance_projections' moduledoc explicitly states its schema is event-store scope (this requirement) while its meaningful population is EE-01/S3 scope, not built here

result.summary: Independently read lib/letflow/design/req023-event-store-schema.md in full (all 1184 lines, commit 2f7a8b8) and re-derived every verdict from the primary sources it cites -- CODE-DESIGNER's step-01 result.summary was not used as evidence for anything. REQ-023's 5 acceptance criteria were grepped verbatim out of docs/requirements.yaml lines 969-973 and match the handoff's task.acceptance_criteria byte-for-byte; REQ-023's full description (lines 898-974) was read clause by clause. VERDICT PASS on all five WF-02 Step 1b checks. (a) Every AC maps to a concrete, non-deferred design element: AC1 -> S4's six named migration files with module names, ordering constraints and exact :prefix placement, S2.2's guard pattern, S5.2's registration manifest, and S4's closing information_schema demonstration method incl. the negative check against public; AC2 -> S3.1's column table (event_id and created_at both primary_key: true) + the Primary key paragraph + INV-EV-2; AC3 -> S5.1's normative absent-function table + S7.1's verbatim moduledoc + INV-EV-1; AC4 -> S3.5's uq_event_idempotency_key unique index + S7.2's verbatim moduledoc; AC5 -> S7.3's verbatim moduledoc + S3.3's concrete list of deferred engine columns. grep -niE 'TBD|to be implemented|to be decided|will be decided later|decide later|FIXME|XXX|placeholder' over the artefact returns ZERO hits. (b) Signatures are fully specified: S5.1 gives @type t and a full @spec for insert_changeset/2 on all six schema modules plus update_changeset/2 and terminal?/1 on InstanceProjection, each with its cast list, validate_required list, validate_length/validate_number bounds and named unique_constraint/foreign_key_constraint targets; S5.2 gives tenant_scoped_migrations/0's @spec. (c) Error shape is stated, not implicit: S5.1 states explicitly that these functions return Ecto.Changeset.t() carrying valid?: false plus field errors and that the {:ok, struct} | {:error, changeset} boundary is Repo.insert/2's inside REQ-025/026 -- an explicit, justified position rather than an omission, consistent with docs/guides/backend_developer_guide.md 3.5 (read, lines 120-127: 'Every @spec states the error shape -- don't leave it implicit'). S2.1/S2.4 restate replay_migrations/2's {:ok, [version]} | {:error, :tenant_not_provisioned} | {:error, {:migration_failed, Exception.t()}} shape. (d) Cross-module dependencies: S8's table names 10 dependencies with direction and nature (Letflow.Repo, TenantProvisioning, Registration, Ecto.Migrator, priv/repo/migrations, REQ-024/025/026, S3/EE-01, security-invariants INV-7); the REQ-024/025/026 characterisations were confirmed against requirements.yaml 976-1040, 1042-1091, 1093-1139. (e) No implementation code: grep -nE '^\s*(def |defp |defmodule |use |import |alias )' and grep -nE '\bdef(module|p)? ' over the artefact BOTH return zero hits; all 14 code fences are untagged and contain only @spec/@type/field(...) declarations, pseudo-code shapes (colon-terminated 'for each'/'unless'/'return' lines that are not valid Elixir), or SQL SELECTs for the demonstration method. === RE-DERIVATION 1, the REQ-022 defect claim: CONFIRMED REAL, and fixing it is IN SCOPE, not scope creep. === Read deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/migrator.ex directly: migrations_for/1 (660-673) turns a {version, module} tuple into {version, module, module}; load_migration!/1's atom clause (725-731) raises Ecto.MigrationError 'module ... is not an Ecto.Migration' unless migration?/1 is true; migration?/1 (744-746) is exactly Code.ensure_loaded?(mod) and function_exported?(mod, :__migration__, 0); the file-path clause (733-742) uses Code.compile_file/1; and line 457 (migrate(Enum.map(pending, &load_migration!/1), ...), preceded by ensure_no_duplication!(pending) at 456) confirms only migrations surviving the pending filter at 647-651 are ever loaded. mix.exs lines 20-21 are elixirc_paths(:test) -> ["lib", "test/support"] / elixirc_paths(_) -> ["lib"], so priv/repo/migrations/*.exs is genuinely never compiled to a .beam, Code.ensure_loaded?/1 on Letflow.Repo.Migrations.CreateEvents returns false, Ecto.Migrator.run/4 raises, and tenant_provisioning.ex:166-179's try/rescue surfaces it as {:error, {:migration_failed, exception}}. The masking mechanism is also real: mix.exs line 48 is test: ["ecto.create --quiet", "ecto.migrate --quiet", "test"], one VM, so on a FRESH test DB the six migrations are pending, get Code.compile_file'd by the ecto.migrate step and are therefore loaded when a test calls replay_migrations; on a WARM DB nothing is pending, nothing is compiled, and the same call raises. Independent judgement: this blocks REQ-023's own AC1 ('applying cleanly ... via REQ-022's migration-replay mechanism') in exactly the state-dependent way that would ship a latent defect while giving a false green on fresh CI, so core-directives.md's Unblock-Everything ('resolve any problem that blocks full completion of the current task') applies -- and independently, req022-tenant-schema-provisioning.md 3.4/6 (lines 332-338, 441-445) already MANDATES that every REQ-023-onward requirement edits this exact function, so the edit needs no new mandate. I agree with ORCH: in scope. The fix leaves the contract intact -- tenant_provisioning.ex:195's @spec tenant_scoped_migrations() :: [{version :: pos_integer(), module()}] and :153-159's replay_migrations/2 @spec are both unchanged by returning six {version, module} pairs, and the added behaviour is confined to Code.ensure_loaded?/Code.require_file module loading with no Repo call (S5.2 states this). The rejected alternative (directory source) is argued correctly: migrations_for/1's wildcard really is Path.join([directory, "**", "*.{ex,exs}"]) (line 664), so a nested tenant/ subdirectory would still be swept by a plain mix ecto.migrate and would buy no isolation. === RE-DERIVATION 2, the mandatory guard pattern: SPECIFIED FOR ALL SIX, BOTH HALVES. === Read req022-tenant-schema-provisioning.md 4 (lines 340-395) directly: it requires change/0 to branch on Ecto.Migration.prefix()'s truthiness and no-op on the nil branch (369-387), and lines 389-395 state verbatim that both halves are mandatory -- guard without registration is 'inert forever', registration without the guard 'actively corrupts public'. The design's S2.2 states the guard shape for every migration and S4's ':prefix threading' bullets say 'Everything above sits inside the if prefix() do ... end guard; the else branch does nothing whatsoever', with per-index prefix: prefix() and the references(...) prefix-inheritance case called out; S4's opening sentence commits all six to both halves and S5.2 supplies the six-entry manifest in ascending version order, with three hard constraints binding the manifest's integers to the filename prefixes. The shipped reference the design cites was confirmed: test/support/req022_migration_fixture.ex lines 24-30 really do implement def change do / if prefix() do / create table(:req022_demo_marker, primary_key: false, prefix: prefix()). Both halves: PRESENT for all six tables. === RE-DERIVATION 3, the deliberately-absent unique index: JUSTIFICATION HOLDS, NOT A FAIL. === Opened C:\Users\tvolo\dev\ai-dala\R-Co\migrations\1147_par01_events_partitioning.sql directly. Lines 162-163 read verbatim 'uq_event_idempotency (idempotency_key) is deliberately NOT recreated here -- global idempotency now lives in plat_event_idempotency (Migration 2 below)', and lines 192-193 read 'uq_event_archive_idempotency (013's index) is likewise not recreated for the same partition-key reason; plat_event_idempotency supersedes its purpose.' Both removals genuinely happened. Lines 200-207 create plat_event_idempotency (idempotency_key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, event_id, created_at) plus idx_plat_event_idempotency_event; lines 31-46 and 99/111 carry the PER_TENANT classification; 133 and 181 carry PRIMARY KEY (event_id, created_at) on events and events_archive. docs/migration/decisions/0003-ecto-schema-strategy.md's Dimension C was read in full: point 2(b) at lines 275-282 says the single global uq_event_idempotency 'could no longer enforce cross-partition global uniqueness once partitioned, so R-Co introduced a sidecar table ... to carry that invariant instead. Letflow adopts the sidecar-table approach for idempotency from the start (not deferred to partitioning time)' -- S7.2 quotes that clause verbatim and correctly. Critically, AC4 requires the unique index ON THE SIDECAR and the design delivers it: S3.5 specifies uq_event_idempotency_key, unique, on event_idempotency(idempotency_key), so global idempotency uniqueness is NOT lost -- it is relocated to a single enforcement point, which is R-Co's shipped end state (store.zig:586-598 inserts the sidecar row first in the same transaction; 705-727, read directly, records 'No ON CONFLICT clause: PAR-01 removes events' own uq_event_idempotency unique index ... PostgreSQL's ON CONFLICT has nothing to infer an arbiter index from and raises 42P10'). R-Co's own 001_event_store.sql:48-49 uq_event_idempotency and 013_event_archive_idempotency.sql:20-21 uq_event_archive_idempotency, and event_store.md invariants 4 and 5 (lines 280, 282) and Open Question #1 (451-460), do say the opposite -- and the design's S10 C-2 identifies them as obsolete rather than glossing them; both texts were read and say what S10 claims. === The other specific checks. === AC2 expressibility: verified against deps/ecto_sql/lib/ecto/adapters/postgres/connection.ex's pk_definition/2 (1454-1465), which collects EVERY column carrying opts[:primary_key] into one PRIMARY KEY (a, b) clause -- so the design's stated form (create table(..., primary_key: false, prefix: prefix()) with two add ..., primary_key: true columns; S3's conventions bullet + S3.1's table) is exactly what Ecto emits, matching the shipped precedent at priv/repo/migrations/20260816000004_create_users.exs:33-34. Ecto CAN emit this. Also verified for S3.4's composite FK: reference_expr/3 (1862-1863) unzips [{name, ref.column} | ref.with] into the composite FOREIGN KEY (event_id, event_created_at) REFERENCES events (event_id, created_at) form, and 1872's Keyword.get(ref.options, :prefix, table.prefix) confirms the reference really does inherit the referencing table's prefix; Ecto.Migration.references/2 documents the :with option at migration.ex:1552-1561, fragment/1 exists at 1325, timestamps/1's :inserted_at rename and :updated_at false are real options (1366-1376), and %Index{} carries where/prefix/unique/name (431-449). Type mapping at 2058-2074 confirms :binary_id->uuid, :string->varchar, :map->jsonb, :bigserial->bigserial, :utc_datetime_usec->timestamp, and 1819-1833 confirms :utc_datetime_usec with no :precision emits a bare timestamp (so S3.1.4's DB-type statement is accurate; config/ has no migration_timestamps, confirmed by grep). Moduledoc text for AC3/AC4/AC5: S7.1/7.2/7.3 give full verbatim paragraphs, not paraphrase instructions, each naming the exact citation its AC demands (Decision C point 1; Decision C point 2(b) plus 'Open Question #1' plus the two-phase check; event-store scope vs. EE-01/S3 population). A later validator can grep these literally. S7.4 adds four further required moduledoc claims. Concrete enough: YES. tenant_id additions: JUSTIFIED, not unrequested scope. 0003 Decision B (lines 37-45) retains 'tenant_id columns ... on the tables the adp-0x docs describe'; R-Co's 027_adp01_event_store_tenant.sql lines 4-10 add tenant_id to events and events_archive and 028_adp02_tenant_scope_persistence.sql lines 18-19 add it to instance_projections -- exactly the three tables the design adds it to. It correctly does NOT add tenant_id to instance_sequence, event_payload_store or event_idempotency, matching R-Co's own 1147 DDL for those tables (no tenant_id there). The design also correctly drops R-Co's DEFAULT '00000000-...' backfill default, since Letflow has no reserved default-tenant UUID. :bigserial for global_seq: the stated reason holds. connection.ex:2062 maps :bigserial -> 'bigserial', so Ecto emits the column inside CREATE TABLE "tenant_xxxx"."events", and Postgres creates a serial column's owning sequence in the same schema as its table -- the sequence does land inside the tenant schema, with no prefix threading and no execute/2 raw SQL (which is also what keeps INV-EV-13 true). The naming divergence IS disclosed: S3.1.1's 'Stated divergence' paragraph records that the generated sequence is events_global_seq_seq rather than R-Co's events_global_seq (R-Co's CREATE SEQUENCE is at 001_event_store.sql:43, still referenced at 1147:131). Open questions: all 7 are genuinely open and NONE blocks an acceptance criterion. OQ-1 -- grepping docs/requirements.yaml for 'retention' returns only lines 1125-1127 (inside REQ-026's description); no requirement creates event_retention_policies, which R-Co creates at 003_event_archive.sql:35-52. Genuinely unowned; REQ-023's six-table scope excludes it and no AC names it. OQ-2 -- R-Co offers no precedent because Store.archive() really is retired (store.zig:1289-1310, read: 'Store.archive() (ES-07's row-level archival-move mechanics) has been REMOVED'); the design still DECIDES on_delete: :restrict rather than deferring, so it is a forward question for REQ-026, not a hole in this design. OQ-3/OQ-4 -- 0003 defers partitioning at lines 264-272 and nothing addresses a cross-tenant stream; both scoped out. OQ-5 -- config/ has no migration_timestamps and grepping the backend guide and every decision record for timestamptz/utc_datetime returns zero hits, so no source already settles it; REQ-023 itself fixes :utc_datetime_usec (line 917), so no AC is affected. OQ-6 -- REQ-024 itself flags the classification open at requirements.yaml:1023-1033. OQ-7 -- an informational forward dependency, not a question. Citation spot-check: roughly 35 of the design's file:line citations were opened and confirmed across 0003, req022's design, tenant_provisioning.ex, mix.exs, four ecto/ecto_sql source files, R-Co's 001/003/012/013/027/028/1147 SQL, store.zig, platform.zig, par-01's design doc and event_store.md. Every one was accurate; no fabricated citation was found. The only imprecision worth naming: the 2(a) quote is cited as 0003:273-277 while the quoted sentence actually spans 272-275 (275-277 begins 2(b)) -- immaterial, the quoted words are verbatim correct. Three MINOR, non-blocking observations are recorded in result.issues; none is a Step 1b check failure and none re-files ISS-0012/0013/0014.

issues.description: events_archive.created_at would inherit events' column default. S3.6 says events_archive carries events' column list 'with the same types, nullability and defaults' and lists only two differences (global_seq, archived_at), so created_at keeps default: fragment("(now() AT TIME ZONE 'utc')"). R-Co gives that column NO default on the archive table (003_event_archive.sql:15 and 1147_par01_events_partitioning.sql:176 both declare created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL with no DEFAULT, unlike events itself), precisely because the archive value is copied from the source row. A default there means a REQ-026 archive insert that omitted created_at would silently stamp archive-time instead of event-time -- and created_at is half the composite primary key, so the corrupted row would still insert cleanly. Recommend ELIXIR-DEV omit the default on events_archive.created_at (null: false only). Not an acceptance-criterion failure: no REQ-023 AC constrains it.

event_payload_store.payload is specified as Ecto :map (jsonb, S3.4) while REQ-023's own description (docs/requirements.yaml:934) offers 'text/bytea'. The design discloses the divergence and cites R-Co's actual type in both revisions (012_event_retention.sql:19 and 1147:219 are both payload JSONB NOT NULL), plus read-time splice type-uniformity with events.payload. No acceptance criterion constrains this column's type and the rationale is sourced, so it is not a gate failure -- recorded so REVIEWER's Step 2d decision-record/scope-consistency check has it explicitly on the record rather than meeting it first in the diff.

S5.2 adds module-loading behaviour (Code.ensure_loaded?/Code.require_file over a filename manifest) to Letflow.TenantProvisioning.tenant_scoped_migrations/0 and correctly notes the @spec (lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex:195) is unchanged -- independently verified. It does not, however, say that the function's shipped @doc (tenant_provisioning.ex:183-194) should be extended to describe the new loading step and why it is required; left unstated, the shipped doc will keep describing a pure list-returning function that now also loads code. Recommend ELIXIR-DEV update that @doc alongside the edit. Separately: req022-tenant-schema-provisioning.md 3.4/4 named the {version, module} mechanism without accounting for migration modules never being compiled (mix.exs:20-21) -- the design flags this as a MINOR against REQ-022's design doc and the gap is independently confirmed real; it is a documentation defect in that earlier artefact, not in this one.
